findings.issue: Under the explicit heading "Added acid (H⁺)", the unqualified "Yes" for any salt containing a weak-acid or weak-base ion misleadingly blurs general pH sensitivity with a response to added acid. Acid increases solubility through this mechanism only when it consumes a dissolved product ion. As a standard-chemistry counterexample, if the pH-active ion is NH₄⁺, added OH⁻ consumes it to form NH₃ and water; added H⁺ does not, so acid need not increase solubility. Make this row conditional and require the dissolution equation to establish whether H⁺ removes an ion and in which direction solubility changes.
findings.evidence: Source 8.11 says acid can increase the solubility of salts containing basic anions or hydroxide, and its answer move is to ask whether H⁺ or OH⁻ removes a dissolved ion. It does not support a blanket response to added acid for every weak-acid or weak-base ion.
